quote: Corollary 3.3. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), and let T be any random variable which is independent of X and Y. Then we have Xn:n^T ≥rh Yn:n^T.

quote: Theorem 3.1. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if µi ≥ µi*, we have Xn:n ≥lr Yn:n.
family: Gumbel distribution Gum(µ,σ): F(x) = exp(−e^{−(x−µ)/σ}), location µ ∈ R, scale σ > 0; independent components
compared: maxima Xn:n vs Yn:n; componentwise location ordering

hypotheses.text: Xi ~ Gum(µi,σ), Yi ~ Gum(µi*,σ) independent; common σ

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), we have Xn:n ≥rh Yn:n.
compared: maxima Xn:n vs Yn:n; majorization of location vectors

hypotheses.formal: µ majorizes µ* (µ more spread); reversed hazard of maximum is Schur-convex in µ
